original_test_intent: Change one defined thermal-limit policy on the intended BMC through an authenticated remote route, verify exact persistence and bounded thermal effect, and restore the full baseline through a path that survives OOB session loss.
original_method: Preserve the TBD source and prohibit execution until a vendor/corrected contract defines remote setter/getter semantics, target identity, secret-safe access, value/safety oracle and independent recovery.
manual_activity: The owners approve the exact thermal object, remote setter/getter, endpoint identity, cipher/secret path, units/range, baseline, requested value, safe effect envelope, dedicated SUT, alternate console/power fallback and full restore.
required_inputs: Vendor thermal-limit application note or corrected testcase
Exact OOB setter/getter and payload schema
Thermal object, component and policy scope
Units, encoding, valid range and reserved fields
BMC endpoint bound to immutable SUT identity
Approved cipher and secret-safe credential source
Complete baseline and exact requested/restore values
Thermal/workload oracle plus independent fallback and recovery owner
safety_requirements: No write while source remains TBD
Never infer from DCMI power commands
One approved write and no automatic retry
Restore without depending solely on the modified OOB path
agent_execution_scope: Bind endpoint and thermal object to intended hardware
Validate exact requested and restore payloads
Issue one remote write after approval
Read back and observe bounded effect
engineer_actions: Approve semantics, endpoint, exact value, safety envelope and independent recovery
Confirm platform protection is not weakened beyond limits

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Resolve the placeholder into an identity-bound, secret-safe and reversible remote thermal-policy transaction with independent monitoring and fallback recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines protocol, identity, safety, evidence and recovery prerequisites while keeping the undefined write non-executable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The IB setter does not test remote attribution/session failure; temperature getters do not authorize policy mutation; power setters do not establish thermal semantics.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong-target or mis-scaled write can weaken protection, throttle or shut down hardware; the thermal effect may disrupt LANPlus and strand an unsafe value without independent access.

project_override_considerations: A Redfish/vendor setter is acceptable only with immutable target proof, same thermal object/effect, exact readback and fallback restoration; omitted LANPlus/raw coverage must be disclosed.
expected_evidence: Authoritative OOB setter/getter artifact and corrected criteria
Immutable SUT/BMC endpoint and redacted secret-safe session
Defined thermal object, units, range and payload schema
One remote set response plus complete readback
Bounded temperature, throttling, workload and SEL/system evidence
Independent restoration and final target/session/system health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title identifies an OOB thermal-limit setter while Procedure and Criteria are placeholders. The source is incomplete but contains no competing asserted method or result.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The remote write purpose is identifiable. The vendor artifact, endpoint, value, safety oracle and recovery are concrete prerequisites; BLOCKED applies only if they remain indeterminate or contradictory after supply.

review_improvement: Defines a safe route from an undefined remote thermal setter to a target-bound, monitored and independently recoverable transaction.
independent_technical_reasoning: The remote route couples two hazards: changing protection semantics and relying on a network management plane that the resulting throttle, shutdown or BMC instability may disrupt. A vendor artifact must first define the exact thermal object and encoding. Then immutable target proof, secret-safe access, independent sensors and an alternate recovery path are required before the one allowed write. Readback over the same session alone cannot prove recoverability or safe hardware behavior.
